summary.text: 右 is the ordinary character for “right,” including the right hand or right-hand side. Its older construction is disputed: it may show a hand with a mouth or ritual vessel, or derive from 又 with 口 added later to distinguish the graph. The evidence here does not settle the choice.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One analysis treats 右 as a compound of 又, a right hand, and 口, a ritual prayer vessel, with a ritual-assistance sense. Another treats 又 as the earlier graph and 口 as a later differentiating mark; a further phonosemantic analysis assigns 又 a sound role and 口 a meaning role. These accounts cannot be combined into a single established construction, and the evidence does not securely establish 又 as a phonetic component inside 右.

components.text: One proposed analysis identifies 又 as a right hand, contributing a depicted hand to a ritual scene. A competing analysis treats it as the earlier graph for 右; another assigns it a phonetic role. The graphic evidence supplied does not resolve these identities or roles.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin 又 yòu and 右 yòu match, and the supplied Baxter–Sagart rows give comparable Old Chinese forms. These readings support a possible sound comparison but do not independently establish 又’s identity as a component or its phonetic role in 右.

components.text: A disputed reading treats 口 as the mouth paired with the hand in the Shuowen account. Another identifies it as a ritual prayer vessel. The view that it was only a differentiating mark is also reported, but not established by the supplied paleographic evidence.

history.text: 右 and 又 are reported in oracle-bone and bronze-script traditions, with later manuscript and script forms also catalogued. The catalogues supplied here do not date the oracle-bone specimen or establish a precise sequence of graphic changes; no historical glyph image was available for inspection.

The received Shuowen explanation reads the graph as a hand and mouth acting together, and survives in versions with different component order. Later commentary and another scholarly account dispute that as the original construction; the textual variants do not resolve the graph’s formation.

One account says 右 was first written with 又 as a whole sign and that 口 was added later to distinguish it. A competing account assigns 口 a ritual meaning, while another analysis calls it semantic and 又 phonetic. The available evidence does not verify a graphic transition or settle these competing explanations.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not securely establish the earliest attested meaning or a chronological chain linking direction, assistance, blessing, ritual service, rank, west, or banquet-related uses. Dictionary citations and inscription catalogues are insufficient to assign priority among these senses.

A whole-graph borrowing account proposes that 又 was reused to write the word for “right” because of sound similarity. But the old object-name and sound match are not independently established here, and evidence for such whole-graph borrowing does not by itself prove that 又 is a phonetic component within 右.

senses.gloss: right; right hand or right-hand side
senses.text: The character is recorded for right hand and right side, but the supplied evidence does not identify either as its earliest sense.
Classical citations record uses for helping or assisting; they are not independently dated here to establish priority or a development from the directional sense.
Dictionary records include blessing or protection uses, without establishing their chronology or a semantic link to direction or assistance.
West is recorded as a sense of the character; the evidence supplied does not date its emergence or explain its relation to “right.”
High status or rank is recorded among historical uses, with no chronology or development established here.
A banquet-related use is recorded and glossed as 侑. The evidence does not establish that this is a semantic extension rather than a distinct word written with 右.
The modern political sense is recorded in the supplied character definitions; no date or semantic-development account is supplied.

limitations.text: The listed senses are attested in dictionary records, but the dossier does not establish the earliest Chinese use or a chronological semantic sequence among them.

If 又 was borrowed as a whole graph for a word meaning “right,” the mechanism would be reuse of the written sign because the words sounded alike or similar, not a meaning change from “also” to “right.” The old name and sound match are not independently established here.

overview.text: 右 is the common character for “right,” including the right hand or right-hand side. Its older construction is disputed: one account sees a hand and mouth or ritual vessel; another says 口 was added to distinguish it from 又.

components.text: 又 may depict a hand in a ritual scene; another account treats it as the earlier graph for 右. Its role in the character remains disputed.
口 is read as a mouth in one traditional explanation, a ritual vessel in another, or a later distinguishing mark in a competing account.

relationships.text: A competing analysis treats 又 as the depiction of a right hand within a ritual scene in 右.

One analysis assigns 又 a phonetic role in 右. Comparable supplied readings make a sound comparison possible, but the readings do not independently confirm the component identity or role; another account treats 又 as an earlier whole graph instead.
One interpretation identifies 口 as a ritual prayer vessel in 右; this is distinct from the account that treats it as a mouth or as a differentiating mark.
A phonosemantic analysis assigns 口 a meaning contribution in 右. The evidence does not show that this is the same analysis as the ritual-vessel interpretation.
One account describes 口 as a later mark added to distinguish 右 from 又; the graphic transition is not independently established in the supplied evidence.
